# 2017B Question 3 {.unnumbered}

::: {.exam-question}
## Question {.question-label}

a) [**Describe**]{.task-verb} the immediate cardiovascular responses to the sudden loss of 30% of the blood volume in a healthy awake person

b) [**How are**]{.task-verb} these responses different if the patient is undergoing anaesthesia with sevoflurane?
:::

Also asked in: [2020B Question 1](/content/exams/anzca/2020/B/1/index.qmd#examiner-comments)

:::: {#answer-structure}

## Suggested Structure

[**Describe**]{.task-verb} the immediate cardiovascular effects and compensatory responses to the specified blood loss in the awake person. Explain [**how**]{.task-verb} sevoflurane modifies those responses through its cardiovascular actions and baroreceptor effects.

## Examiner Comments

::: {.examiner-comments}
**67.5%** of candidates achieved a pass in this question

The two parts of the question carried the same weight. A good answer to the first part included the effects on the cardiovascular system as a result of a 30% loss of blood volume, followed by the various compensation mechanisms. Detailed anatomical descriptions of the sympathetic and parasympathetic nervous systems were not required.

The focus of the second part of the question should be on the pharmacodynamics effects of sevoflurane on the cardiovascular system, and how these effects will be exacerbated in a patient with hypovolaemia. Better candidates demonstrated understanding that sevoflurane blunts the responsiveness of baroreceptors in a dose dependent manner. Discussions on the effects of intravenous anaesthesia, mechanical ventilation or the treatment of hypotension did not attract marks.
:::
